newsitem.title: ITALY: SOCCER-WEAH READY TO APOLOGISE FOR BUTT.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-WEAH READY TO APOLOGISE FOR BUTT.

text.p: George Weah said on Friday that he was ready to apologise to Porto captain Jorge Costa, saying he had been "stupid" to have broken his nose after racist provocation.

The Liberian, who butted Costa in the players' tunnel after the November 20 European Champions' League match, also said he was interested in moving to Arsenal if AC Milan decided he was no longer needed.
"I am ready to publicly apologise to Costa, to hold out my hand first, wherever and whenever he and UEFA wish," the world player of the year was quoted as saying in Friday's La Gazzetta dello Sport.
UEFA suspended Weah for Milan's vital final Champions' League clash against Rosenborg next week and said it would conduct a full investigation later.
Costa underwent surgery last week and is expected to be out of action for at least three weeks.
Weah, speaking publicly for the first time about the incident, said that his only condition would be for Costa to admit he had been provoking him.
"Just as I admit my reaction, I would like, however, him to admit his provocation. Nobody can think that I am a madman, that I attacked him without being heavily provoked," he said.
Weah suggested that both he and Costa should play in a friendly in Lisbon scheduled for January 29 between African and European players as a goodwill gesture.
The striker, due to be awarded FIFA's 1996 Fair Play award at a ceremony in Lisbon in January, said 10 years of good behaviour in Europe should not be cancelled by one incident.
He said Costa had committed a dangerous foul on him during the match that could have ended his career but he had suppressed any instinct to react at the time.
"But when in the tunnel Costa began to insult me, to shout 'Negro' at me and do monkey imitations I could no longer keep my self-control. I now apologise to him.

"It may seem ridiculous to say it and hear it but I swear I did not mean him harm. When I saw his blood, I was shocked and I ran away," Weah told the newspaper, adding that he was ready to make a formal apology and shake Costa's hand.
Weah said that he had become accustomed to racist comments from the crowd, saying that denigrating an opponent was merely a way in which supporters backed their own team.
But he said he had been shocked by Costa's attitude to him on the pitch in Milan's two clashes with Porto.

"Look at the film. Not once did he say sorry after every foul or help me get back to my feet. In Milan and Oporto he treated me like an animal, hitting me without even addressing a word to me. He just turned away and carried on."
Weah said that if Milan, who have supported him wholeheartedly over the incident, decided to sell him before his contract expired in 1999 it would not be a disaster.
"The club knows that Arsenal has made a good offer for me and if they decided to accept it and invest the money in younger players it would be quite understood," he told the newspaper.
"As far as I am concerned, I would be happy to join Arsene Wenger again. It could be a good deal for everybody."

Wenger was Weah's first coach in Europe at Monaco and the Liberian has made no secret in the past that he feels he owes a huge debt to the thoughtful French coach who moved to the English premier league club from Japan this season.

When Weah was awarded the player of the year prize in Milan last January, he invited Wenger up on to the stage and told the audience: "I want you all to know I love a lot of people, but a good man has to be rewarded. This is the man.
"When I came to Europe, you were like a father to me."
